title: 359. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Perimeter of Composite Figures
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the perimeter of an L-shaped figure formed by removing a square from a corner.
questions.question: A \(3\text{ cm}\) by \(3\text{ cm}\) square has a \(1\text{ cm}\) by \(1\text{ cm}\) square removed from one corner. What is the perimeter of the resulting L-shaped figure?
questions.explanation:
Trace the outer boundary of the L-shaped figure. The side lengths around the boundary are \(3\), \(2\), \(1\), \(1\), \(2\), and \(3\text{ cm}\). Their sum is
\[
3+2+1+1+2+3=12.
\]
Therefore, the perimeter is \(12\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Trace only the outer boundary of the remaining figure, including the two new edges created by the removed corner.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the perimeter of two rectangles joined along a full side.
questions.question: A \(6\text{ cm}\) by \(2\text{ cm}\) rectangle and a \(6\text{ cm}\) by \(3\text{ cm}\) rectangle are joined along their \(6\text{ cm}\) sides to form one composite figure. What is the perimeter of the composite figure?
questions.explanation:
Joining the two rectangles along a \(6\text{ cm}\) side forms a larger rectangle with dimensions \(6\text{ cm}\) by \(2+3=5\text{ cm}\). The shared \(6\text{ cm}\) side is internal and is not part of the perimeter. Thus,
\[
P=2(6+5)=22.
\]
So the perimeter is \(22\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Find the dimensions of the larger rectangle first, then use the rectangle perimeter formula.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the effect of removing a corner rectangle on perimeter.
questions.question: An \(8\text{ cm}\) by \(5\text{ cm}\) rectangle has a \(2\text{ cm}\) by \(3\text{ cm}\) rectangle removed from one corner. What is the perimeter of the remaining composite figure?
questions.explanation:
The original rectangle has perimeter
\[
2(8+5)=26.
\]
Removing a rectangle from a corner removes two outer segments, but it adds two new inner edges of the same total length. Therefore, the perimeter is unchanged. The perimeter remains \(26\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Compare the lengths removed from the outer boundary with the new lengths exposed by the corner cut.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the perimeter of a rectangle with a semicircle attached to one side.
questions.question: A semicircle is attached to one \(8\text{ cm}\) side of an \(8\text{ cm}\) by \(4\text{ cm}\) rectangle, with the \(8\text{ cm}\) side as the diameter. What is the perimeter of the composite figure?
questions.explanation:
The attached \(8\text{ cm}\) side is internal. The exposed rectangle sides are the opposite \(8\text{ cm}\) side and the two \(4\text{ cm}\) sides:
\[
8+4+4=16.
\]
The semicircle has radius \(4\text{ cm}\), so its arc length is
\[
\pi r=4\pi.
\]
Thus, the perimeter is \(16+4\pi\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Count only the exposed rectangle sides and the semicircular arc.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the perimeter of a square attached to a rectangle along a full side.
questions.question: A \(5\text{ cm}\) by \(5\text{ cm}\) square is attached to one \(5\text{ cm}\) side of an \(8\text{ cm}\) by \(5\text{ cm}\) rectangle. The square shares the entire \(5\text{ cm}\) side with the rectangle. What is the perimeter of the composite figure?
questions.explanation:
The composite figure is a larger rectangle with width \(8+5=13\text{ cm}\) and height \(5\text{ cm}\). The shared \(5\text{ cm}\) side is internal and is not counted. Therefore,
\[
P=2(13+5)=36.
\]
So the perimeter is \(36\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: The two shapes form a larger rectangle; identify its total length and width.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the perimeter of a rectangle combined with a right triangle.
questions.question: A right triangle with legs \(6\text{ cm}\) and \(8\text{ cm}\) is attached to a \(6\text{ cm}\) by \(4\text{ cm}\) rectangle along the \(6\text{ cm}\) leg. What is the perimeter of the composite figure?
questions.explanation:
The shared \(6\text{ cm}\) leg is internal. The exposed rectangle sides are \(6\), \(4\), and \(4\text{ cm}\). The triangle contributes its other leg \(8\text{ cm}\) and its hypotenuse. Since the legs are \(6\text{ cm}\) and \(8\text{ cm}\), the hypotenuse is
\[
\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\text{ cm}.
\]
Thus, the perimeter is
\[
6+4+4+8+10=32\text{ cm}.
\]
questions.hint: The shared side is not part of the perimeter; find the hypotenuse of the right triangle.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the perimeter of a rectangle with a semicircular notch.
questions.question: A semicircular notch of diameter \(6\text{ cm}\) is cut from one \(6\text{ cm}\) side of a \(10\text{ cm}\) by \(6\text{ cm}\) rectangle. What is the perimeter of the remaining figure?
questions.explanation:
The side containing the notch is replaced by a semicircular arc. The remaining straight outer sides are
\[
10+10+6=26.
\]
The notch has radius \(3\text{ cm}\), so its arc length is
\[
\pi r=3\pi.
\]
Therefore, the perimeter is \(26+3\pi\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: The notched side is replaced by a semicircular arc; use the notch radius, not the diameter, for the arc length.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the perimeter of a rectangle with semicircles attached to opposite sides.
questions.question: Semicircles are attached outward to both \(4\text{ cm}\) sides of an \(8\text{ cm}\) by \(4\text{ cm}\) rectangle. What is the perimeter of the composite figure?
questions.explanation:
The two \(8\text{ cm}\) sides remain exposed, giving length
\[
8+8=16.
\]
Each semicircle has radius \(2\text{ cm}\). The two semicircles together form a full circle of radius \(2\text{ cm}\), whose circumference is
\[
2\pi r=2\pi(2)=4\pi.
\]
Thus, the perimeter is \(16+4\pi\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: The two semicircular arcs combine to form one full circle.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the perimeter after cutting a quarter-circle from a rectangle corner.
questions.question: A quarter-circle of radius \(4\text{ cm}\) is cut from one corner of a \(12\text{ cm}\) by \(8\text{ cm}\) rectangle. What is the perimeter of the remaining figure?
questions.explanation:
The original rectangle has perimeter
\[
2(12+8)=40\text{ cm}.
\]
Cutting the corner removes two straight segments of length \(4\text{ cm}\) each, so subtract \(8\text{ cm}\). The new boundary includes a quarter-circle arc of radius \(4\text{ cm}\):
\[
\frac{1}{4}(2\pi r)=\frac{1}{4}(2\pi\cdot 4)=2\pi.
\]
Thus, the perimeter is
\[
40-8+2\pi=32+2\pi\text{ cm}.
\]
questions.hint: Subtract the two straight corner segments that are removed, then add the quarter-circle arc length.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the perimeter of a rectangle with two semicircles attached to different sides.
questions.question: A semicircle of radius \(3\text{ cm}\) is attached to one \(6\text{ cm}\) side of a \(10\text{ cm}\) by \(6\text{ cm}\) rectangle. A semicircle of radius \(5\text{ cm}\) is attached to one \(10\text{ cm}\) side. What is the perimeter of the composite figure?
questions.explanation:
The two attached sides are internal. The remaining exposed rectangle sides are the other \(6\text{ cm}\) side and the other \(10\text{ cm}\) side:
\[
6+10=16.
\]
The semicircular arc lengths are
\[
3\pi
\]
and
\[
5\pi.
\]
Their sum is \(8\pi\). Therefore, the perimeter is \(16+8\pi\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Add the two exposed straight sides of the rectangle and the two semicircular arc lengths.
